scope: Local Windows 11 x64, real MSVC/Tauri/WebView2 executable using a dedicated test identifier and a generated loopback SSH/SFTP endpoint.
feature: A02/A09: reviewed SFTP queues can recover never-started entries after process exit.
observations: Normal window close with a paused two-entry queue preserved the one undispatched item. Offline removal kept its independent transfer receipt.

Force-terminating the process during the first download of a three-file batch left one unconfirmed receipt. Offline review identified exactly two pending files. Viewing the queue and reopening the app added zero authentication attempts.

A changed host key, directory replaced at the same path, stale review revision, concurrent second writer, and a transfer whose endpoint differed from its reviewed entry each failed before a file could be transferred.
After interactive reconnect and confirmation, both pending files matched the originals byte for byte. The interrupted file remained unpublished. The exhausted queue disappeared.
Fixed standalone browser_smoke compilation by passing the optional quote-engine revision callback from the desktop builder. The browser-only target requires no Agent state.

tests.standaloneBrowser: cargo run --bin browser_smoke: native popup, layout, tab identity, settings, cache, download, extensions and isolation checks passed

limits: Only explicitly saved pending entries are recoverable. Partial-file byte checkpoints and tokens stay in-process. An interrupted published result must be checked in workspace history.
Uploads read the current contents at reviewed paths. Durable mode requires a recognizable local directory identity.
Pre-feature in-memory queues cannot be reconstructed.
releaseGates: Clean Windows 10 and Windows 11 acceptance and an authenticated production-provider turn remain separate from local preview verification.
